prs.short_reason: [llm] cluster primary: Client tool calls hang forever because _handle_post_request never sends an error back through read_stream_writer when the POST to the server fails or returns a bad response (connection dies/server crash in #1578; non-2xx HTTP status in #3092) — the waiting caller is left with no response at all. prs.cluster_pick_reason: #1578's diff rewrites the entire _handle_post_request body (-47/+61 lines) around the same 'if response.status_' line that #3092 targets, and introduces a reusable _send_error_response helper that funnels any POST-path failure — connection errors and non-2xx status alike — into a JSON-RPC error on read_stream_writer. #3092's visible diff only adds new imports (pydantic ValidationError, INTERNAL_ERROR) for a status-check fix in that same function, so its non-2xx handling is a subset of what #1578's broader rewrite already covers.

prs.title: fix: terminate active StreamableHTTP sessions during shutdown
prs.author: weiguangli-io
prs.reason: [llm] cluster primary: Active StreamableHTTP SSE streams (EventSourceResponse coroutines) are cancelled mid-stream when the session manager shuts down instead of completing gracefully, which is what causes Uvicorn to log ASGI-incomplete-response errors. Both PRs' titles state the identical goal ('terminate active StreamableHTTP sessions during shutdown' vs 'terminate streamable HTTP sessions on manager shutdown'), and both work by tracking SSE stream writers in self._sse_stream_writers so they can be closed on termination. (2 PRs)
prs.short_reason: [llm] cluster primary: Active StreamableHTTP SSE streams (EventSourceResponse coroutines) are cancelled mid-stream when the session manager shuts down instead of completing gracefully, which is what causes Uvicorn to log ASGI-incomplete-response errors. Both PRs' titles state the identical goal ('terminate active StreamableHTTP sessions during shutdown' vs 'terminate streamable HTTP sessions on manager shutdown'), and both work by tracking SSE stream writers in self._sse_stream_writers so they can be closed on termination. (2 PRs)
prs.cluster_pick_reason: PR #2253 implements both halves of the fix: it adds the actual close-loop over self._sse_stream_writers inside terminate() in streamable_http.py (the mechanism that makes any registered writer closeable), and it updates streamable_http_manager.py's lifespan shutdown to call session termination before cancelling tasks. PR #3218's diff only adds registration of the GET-request stream into self._sse_stream_writers in streamable_http.py - that registration is inert without a closing loop in terminate(), and #3218 does not touch streamable_http_manager.py at all, so it addresses only one piece of the shutdown-ordering problem. If #3218's GET-stream registration isn't already covered by #2253's scope, that one hunk should be ported into #2253 rather than merging both PRs.

prs.author: MukundaKatta
prs.reason: [llm] cluster primary: Both fix the same root cause: pickling an MCPError-family exception fails because the default Exception.__reduce_ex__ reconstructs via cls(*self.args), and self.args (set to (code, message, data) by MCPError.__init__) doesn't match subclass constructor signatures — concretely, UrlElicitationRequiredError(elicitations, message=None) raises TypeError on unpickle. #2555 explicitly references the tracking issue (#2431) for this exact symptom. (2 PRs)

prs.cluster_pick_reason: #2478 fixes this at the MCPError base level via a shared _restore_mcp_error reconstructor that dispatches to each subclass's existing from_error_data/from_error classmethod, so it covers every current and future MCPError subclass through one reconstruction path — and its dispatch explicitly special-cases UrlElicitationRequiredError (calling from_error instead of from_error_data) to correctly rebuild the typed elicitations list, so it also covers #2555's specific case. #2555 only adds a bespoke __reduce__ to the single UrlElicitationRequiredError subclass, which would leave any other MCPError subclass with a non-matching constructor signature still broken, and introduces a second, parallel reconstruction mechanism alongside the from_error_data/from_error path rather than reusing it. #2478 also drops the '# pragma: no cover' on MCPError.data, indicating its change is exercised by a payload round-trip test, whereas #2555's shown diff only adds coverage for the one subclass.

prs.author: arimu1
prs.reason: [llm] cluster primary: Concurrent requests reusing the same JSON-RPC request id can cross-wire or overwrite each other's routing slot in `_request_streams`, since the map is keyed by request id. (2 PRs)
prs.short_reason: [llm] cluster primary: Concurrent requests reusing the same JSON-RPC request id can cross-wire or overwrite each other's routing slot in `_request_streams`, since the map is keyed by request id. (2 PRs)
prs.cluster_pick_reason: #3063 keys `_request_streams` by `str(message.id)` and only checks that string for collisions. #3221's own code comment identifies the resulting bug directly: `str(id)` collapses integer `1` and string `"1"` into the same key, so an in-flight numeric id can falsely 409 a distinct string id (or cross-wire responses), and a string id equal to `GET_STREAM_KEY` (`"_GET_stream"`) could collide with the standalone GET slot. #3221 replaces the naive cast with a type-preserving `_request_stream_key()` (`i:`/`s:` prefixes) that avoids both collision cases while still rejecting genuine duplicate in-flight ids, making it a strict superset of #3063's fix.

prs.title: Fix OAuthClientProvider._initialize() to enable transparent token refresh
prs.author: draesthetic
prs.reason: [llm] cluster primary: OAuthClientProvider never restores token_expiry_time when tokens are reloaded from storage after a restart, so is_token_valid() treats a stale/expired access_token as valid, the proactive refresh branch in async_auth_flow is skipped, and every expiry forces a full interactive re-authorization instead of a silent refresh. (3 PRs)
prs.short_reason: [llm] cluster primary: OAuthClientProvider never restores token_expiry_time when tokens are reloaded from storage after a restart, so is_token_valid() treats a stale/expired access_token as valid, the proactive refresh branch in async_auth_flow is skipped, and every expiry forces a full interactive re-authorization instead of a silent refresh. (3 PRs)
prs.cluster_pick_reason: #3251 contains the identical core fix as #1784 (compute token_expiry_time from the loaded token's expires_in inside _initialize, mirroring what set_tokens already does on the write path) and additionally restores OAuth server metadata via an optional getattr-guarded storage call, so it also covers the related refresh-endpoint-rediscovery gap without requiring a new storage protocol method. #2875 addresses the same diagnosed root cause (its own comment cites token_expiry_time not being restored) but only at the symptom layer inside the 401 branch of async_auth_flow: it still sends the stale token, waits for the 401, and only then attempts a refresh, adding an extra network round-trip and more invasive generator control flow (an early return mid-yield) versus a one-line fix isolated to _initialize.

prs.title: Release context.lock before the protected request is sent
prs.author: guptaishaan
prs.reason: [llm] cluster primary: context.lock is held across the yielded HTTP request/response in async_auth_flow, so a single long-running request (e.g. a standalone GET SSE stream) blocks every other concurrent request against the same OAuthClientProvider for the full duration of that request. (3 PRs)
prs.short_reason: [llm] cluster primary: context.lock is held across the yielded HTTP request/response in async_auth_flow, so a single long-running request (e.g. a standalone GET SSE stream) blocks every other concurrent request against the same OAuthClientProvider for the full duration of that request. (3 PRs)
prs.cluster_pick_reason: #3252's diff is fully visible and shows the complete fix: it moves 'response = yield request' outside any lock and re-acquires context.lock narrowly and symmetrically for both the 401 and 403 handling branches, reusing the existing anyio.Lock with no changes to OAuthContext's fields. #3243 makes a larger, less-verified change by swapping lock for anyio.Semaphore and adding a new flow_lock field to work around cross-task generator resumption, a change in synchronization primitive that isn't shown to be necessary once no lock is held across a yield/suspension point. #2858 adds a second refresh_lock field but is a rebase of an older, previously unmerged community PR (#2660, closes #2847); the actual async_auth_flow scope-narrowing logic isn't present in the diff shown, making its handling of the 401/403 paths harder to verify against the other two.

clusters.pick_reason: #3063 keys `_request_streams` by `str(message.id)` and only checks that string for collisions. #3221's own code comment identifies the resulting bug directly: `str(id)` collapses integer `1` and string `"1"` into the same key, so an in-flight numeric id can falsely 409 a distinct string id (or cross-wire responses), and a string id equal to `GET_STREAM_KEY` (`"_GET_stream"`) could collide with the standalone GET slot. #3221 replaces the naive cast with a type-preserving `_request_stream_key()` (`i:`/`s:` prefixes) that avoids both collision cases while still rejecting genuine duplicate in-flight ids, making it a strict superset of #3063's fix.

members.reason: [llm] cluster primary: context.lock is held across the yielded HTTP request/response in async_auth_flow, so a single long-running request (e.g. a standalone GET SSE stream) blocks every other concurrent request against the same OAuthClientProvider for the full duration of that request. (3 PRs)

members.cluster_pick_reason: #3252's diff is fully visible and shows the complete fix: it moves 'response = yield request' outside any lock and re-acquires context.lock narrowly and symmetrically for both the 401 and 403 handling branches, reusing the existing anyio.Lock with no changes to OAuthContext's fields. #3243 makes a larger, less-verified change by swapping lock for anyio.Semaphore and adding a new flow_lock field to work around cross-task generator resumption, a change in synchronization primitive that isn't shown to be necessary once no lock is held across a yield/suspension point. #2858 adds a second refresh_lock field but is a rebase of an older, previously unmerged community PR (#2660, closes #2847); the actual async_auth_flow scope-narrowing logic isn't present in the diff shown, making its handling of the 401/403 paths harder to verify against the other two.

clusters.pick_reason: #3063 keys `_request_streams` by `str(message.id)` and only checks that string for collisions. #3221's own code comment identifies the resulting bug directly: `str(id)` collapses integer `1` and string `"1"` into the same key, so an in-flight numeric id can falsely 409 a distinct string id (or cross-wire responses), and a string id equal to `GET_STREAM_KEY` (`"_GET_stream"`) could collide with the standalone GET slot. #3221 replaces the naive cast with a type-preserving `_request_stream_key()` (`i:`/`s:` prefixes) that avoids both collision cases while still rejecting genuine duplicate in-flight ids, making it a strict superset of #3063's fix.

members.author: Sammy-Dabbas
members.reason: [llm] duplicates #3221: Concurrent requests reusing the same JSON-RPC request id can cross-wire or overwrite each other's routing slot in `_request_streams`, since the map is keyed by request id.
